To: group:levy-longsight-noticeboard
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Blue pills sold as diazepam/Xanax - please read, and please share

Evening all. I know it's late and I'm shattered - I've just come off nights - but this can't wait.

There's a police warning on this board about fake pills and I don't think it's being read properly, so I'm putting my own post up rather than adding to the Saturday thread. I am not naming anyone, I am not repeating what people are saying about that night, and this post is not about who did what. It is only about the pills and about what to do if it happens to somebody you love.

Blue tablets are being sold in this area as diazepam or Xanax. Some of them contain nitazenes - synthetic opioids - and they can be far stronger than heroin. You cannot tell by looking at one. You cannot tell by looking at the person who took it either. That is the whole danger.

Things to watch for if someone has taken something: extreme drowsiness, pinpoint pupils, slow or noisy breathing, blue lips.

If somebody goes down, ring 999 straight away. Don't put them to bed to sleep it off. Don't wait to see if they wake up. Don't worry about getting in trouble, and don't worry about whether it's "serious enough" - if you think something's wrong, it's wrong enough to ring. The police have said their priority is preserving life. That is their own words, and it is the only thing that matters at two in the morning.

I'll say it plainly, because I see the aftermath of people not ringing early enough in my job. The usual pattern is panic: a mate takes something, their friends panic, they put them in bed, they ring hours later. By then the brain has been without oxygen too long. If you ring at the first sign that someone is not right - even if you're not sure, even if it turns out to be nothing - ring. Nobody will criticise you for calling.

Naloxone: naloxone nasal spray reverses opioids. It is free, you don't need a referral, you don't need to be trained and you don't need to give your name. Brightpath drug and alcohol service on Stockport Road, next to the launderette - free nasal naloxone kits, anyone can walk in and ask, and the training takes about ten minutes. They're open Monday to Friday 10 till 4, and Thursdays until 7.

Parents, please talk to your kids THIS week. Not after half term, not "when it's less awkward". I had that conversation with my own lad (14) last night, over his tea. He rolled his eyes at me - honestly he did - but he listened, and then he asked me what pinpoint pupils meant. That told me more than anything else.

And to the adults slagging the kids off in the thread: it helps nobody, not one bit. Scared kids don't ring for help. That's the whole problem. The ones who most need to pick up a phone are the least likely to, because they're frightened of being told off and because nobody ever made it feel safe to say "I think my friend is in trouble".

So please - parents, talk to your kids this week. Mates, if your friend goes quiet, is hard to wake, or is breathing oddly, ring 999. And please share this post rather than just liking it and scrolling past. If this stops one ambulance being called late, it's worth every word.
